title: How Much Do Investors Care About Macroeconomic Risk? Evidence from Scheduled Economic Announcements
one_line: Excess market returns averaged 11.4 bp on CPI/PPI, employment and FOMC announcement days vs 1.1 bp on other days (difference t = 3.77, 1958-2009): over 60% of the equity premium is earned on ~13% of days, with volatility only ~5% higher.

findings.statement: Announcement days 11.4 bp vs 1.1 bp other days; difference 10.3 bp, t = 3.77; non-announcement returns not different from zero.
Sharpe ratio on announcement days ≈ 10× other days.
Effect holds for each announcement type and survives controls for the size of the surprise.
T-bill yields fall and long bonds earn more on announcement days (precautionary demand).

why.pattern: Risk premium for bearing macro 'state variable' risk that is resolved on announcement days.

reported_results.headline: Excess market returns averaged 11.4 bp on CPI/PPI, employment and FOMC announcement days vs 1.1 bp on other days (difference t = 3.77, 1958-2009): over 60% of the equity premium is earned on ~13% of days, with volatility only ~5% higher.

tradable_edge: New spec macro_announcement_day_long_es: hold ES on CPI/PPI/NFP/FOMC days (prior close → day close, plus RTH-only variant). Complements pre_macro_overnight_es (the night before) and pre_fomc_drift_uncertainty_es.

decay_risk.reason: Old sample; part of the FOMC piece is the pre-FOMC drift that weakened after 2015.

data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 5, 2026-11-10), not by the weekly pipeline.
